venue.name: Raincoast Education Society
venue.description: The Raincoast Education Society is a registered charity based in Ucluelet that runs field-based outdoor education around Tofino and Ucluelet in the Clayoquot and Barkley Sound region. It offers school programs taught by certified educators on topics such as intertidal ecology, rainforest ecology, oceanography and plankton ecology, invertebrate diversity, avian ecology and mudflat ecology, priced per group rather than per child. It also hosts the Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre at Amphitrite Point in Ucluelet from Monday to Friday, and runs a Raincoast Field School partnership that gives every Kindergarten to Grade 7 student at Wickaninnish Community School in Tofino and at Ucluelet Elementary School at least one field trip a month. Its summer day camps for ages 6 to 12 are registered through the Tofino and Ucluelet recreation departments rather than through the society.
venue.hours_notes: The Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre at Amphitrite Point in Ucluelet is open 9:00 am to 4:00 pm every day. Raincoast Education Society hosts it Monday to Friday and the Wild Pacific Trail Society hosts it on Saturday and Sunday. The society's office on Bay Street asks you to call ahead before you drop in.
venue.seasonal_notes: Several of the field topics can only run at low tide, so the date and time depend on the tide rather than on the calendar. The spring and fall mudflat tours focus on shorebird migration.

programs.name: Half day field program
programs.description: A field-based outdoor program of 1.5 to 2 hours, taught by certified educators at sites around Tofino and Ucluelet, for a flat rate of $300 per group. Topics on offer include intertidal ecology, rainforest ecology, oceanography and plankton ecology, invertebrate diversity, avian ecology and mudflat ecology, and the educators build the session around the age and interests of the group. Teaching is tailored to the grade level. Several topics can only run at low tide, and the beach seine also depends on equipment and location, so the date and time you ask for may have to move. Mudflat tours are based at Tofino Botanical Gardens. For avian ecology the site asks groups to bring their own binoculars.
programs.what_children_do: Go out with an educator to a rocky shore, a mudflat or a rainforest and look closely at what lives there. Depending on the topic they search tide pools at low tide, help pull a beach seine through the shallows and look at plankton under a microscope, or walk and watch for songbirds, seabirds and shorebirds with binoculars they bring themselves.
programs.our_note: The price is for the whole group rather than per child, so it is good value for a class of twenty and dear for a group of six. Most of the topics only run at low tide, so ask early and expect to take the date the tide gives you rather than the one you wanted.
programs.practical_summary: You get a certified educator, a flat group rate and a choice of coastal topics. Where you meet, washrooms, lunch, a rain backup, bus parking, how many adults have to come and the youngest age are all unstated, so it is worth an email before you book a bus.
programs.evidence: We offer our 1.5 - 2 hour school programs for a rate of $300 per group

programs.name: Full day field program
programs.description: The longer version of the same field-based programs, running 5 to 6 hours for a flat rate of $600 per group, taught by certified educators at sites around Tofino and Ucluelet. The same topics are available: intertidal ecology, rainforest ecology, oceanography and plankton ecology, invertebrate diversity, avian ecology and mudflat ecology. Most of them can only run at low tide, and the beach seine also depends on equipment and location. The site does not say whether a break or a lunch stop is built into the day.
programs.what_children_do: Spend most of a day outdoors with an educator on the shore, the mudflats or a rainforest trail, working through one topic in depth: searching tide pools, pulling a beach seine, looking at plankton under a microscope, or identifying birds along the coast.
programs.our_note: Five to six hours outdoors on a coastal shore is a long day for younger children, and nothing on the site says where they would eat or shelter. Ask what the day is broken into, and where the group can stop for lunch, before you book this rather than the shorter version.
programs.practical_summary: A full day outdoors with a certified educator at a flat group rate. Lunch, washrooms, a rain backup, the meeting point and how many adults have to come are not published, so settle those by email first.
programs.evidence: a 5 - 6 hour program for $600 per group

programs.name: Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre visit
programs.description: A small museum space at Amphitrite Point in Ucluelet with a different interpretive topic each day. It is open from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm every day. The Raincoast Education Society hosts it Monday to Friday and the Wild Pacific Trail Society hosts it on Saturday and Sunday. The site does not say whether there is an admission charge, whether a group has to book ahead, or how many people the room holds.
programs.what_children_do: Go into a small museum room at Amphitrite Point, look at the displays and hear about whatever the day's topic is from whoever is hosting.
programs.our_note: It is one small room, so treat it as a stop along a walk on the point rather than as the outing itself. Nothing about cost, group size or booking is on the site, so phone before you turn up with twenty children.
programs.practical_summary: Open every day from 9 to 4 at Amphitrite Point, and indoors. Admission, washrooms, parking and whether a group needs to book ahead are all unstated.
programs.evidence: Open from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm everyday at Ucluelet's Amphitrite Point

gaps: no age or grade range is published for the school field programs; the site says only that programs are for visiting elementary and secondary schools and that teaching is tailored to the group's age and grade level
no youngest age is published, so whether daycare and preschool groups are welcome is unknown; the interpretive programs page says programs are designed for all ages but nothing states a minimum
how many adults have to come is unknown: the site says there is a student to educator ratio but never says what it is
months are unknown; the site does not say which months or seasons the school field programs run
no meeting point or pick-up location is published for the field programs. They take place at sites around Tofino and Ucluelet, and the mudflat tours are based at Tofino Botanical Gardens

the address recorded is the society's office at 1801 Bay St in Ucluelet, which the site asks you to call ahead before visiting. It is not where a field program meets, so the map pin should not be read as the outing location
washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site
no lunch space is described, and the site does not say whether a lunch break is built into the 5 to 6 hour program
no rain backup or shelter is described; the field programs are outdoors and most depend on low tide
bus parking is not mentioned anywhere on the site
stroller access and wheelchair access are not mentioned anywhere on the site
no lead time, deposit, payment timing or cancellation policy is published
whether the $300 and $600 rates include GST is not stated, and no year or season is given for them
no admission price is published for the Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre, and it does not say whether a group has to book ahead or how many people the room holds

the Raincoast Field School is described as a standing arrangement with Wickaninnish Community School in Tofino and Ucluelet Elementary School, covering Kindergarten to Grade 7. The site does not say whether any other school can join it, or what it costs, so it is not recorded as a bookable program

the summer day camps for ages 6 to 12 are registered through the Tofino and Ucluelet recreation departments on their own booking sites, not through the society, so they are not recorded as a group program here

the school programs page repeats the intertidal ecology text under the rainforest ecology heading, so the rainforest description on that page is not reliable. The interpretive programs page carries a separate rainforest description

the interpretive programs page asks groups to submit a form hosted off the society's own site. The link was recorded as the booking route only on that page and the record uses the society's own contact page instead

every photograph on the site carries an alt attribute that is the image file name rather than a description.
